pattern.crimePattern: a mother who bought her son a fake school certificate kills the HR manager who found out and was about to report it
pattern.notes: Fictional hospital staff and exam candidates. The certificate's flaw (an index number belonging to someone else) is shown; how such certificates are made is never described. The mother is written with sympathy.

ob.text: A neighbour reports a woman found dead at the gate of her home in Chuka at 22:30, struck on the head. Irene Kagwiria (41), HR manager at the county hospital.

reconstruction.text: Melvin fails his KCSE. His mother, who spent her pension on his schooling, pays a man in Meru KSh 30,000 for a certificate. Its index number belongs to a stranger: Kalekye Muli, a teacher in Kitui.
In March the hospital hires him. On Thursday the exam council tells Irene the number is someone else's. On Friday afternoon she tells Melvin he'll be dismissed and reported on Monday.

About 20:30, in her church headscarf, Philomena goes to Irene's gate to beg. She kneels on the road. Irene says, "I'm sorry, Mama, I can't," and turns away. Philomena picks up a stone from the top of the garden wall.
By 20:55 she is gone. She washes her headscarf and hangs it on the line.

ui.beatNotes: Calling a stranger. The desk phone calls a witness outside the region; Kalekye's photo of her real certificate arrives as a picture message beside the forged one. Same number, different life. The Meru number on Philomena's note goes to the Pattern File as a lead for the forgery market (not a spine thread).
